einzeiler: Novelist Elizabeth Strout on turning 70 and her New England upbringing.
kurzfassung: Novelist Elizabeth Strout discusses turning 70 and her reserved New England upbringing. She explores how death figures into her latest novel, The Things We Never Say. The conversation also covers her late start in publishing, a stand-up comedy class, and her fascination with New York City's emotional straight talk.
stichpunkte: Death in the latest novel, The Things We Never Say
An experience taking a stand-up comedy class
A fascination with New York City's loud, emotional straight talk
beschreibung:
The bestselling novelist behind works like Amy and Isabelle and Olive Kitteridge discusses her excitement about turning 70, her reserved New England upbringing, and how death figures into her latest novel, The Things We Never Say. She also talks about her later start in publishing, her experience taking a stand-up comedy class, and her fascination with New York City’s loud, emotional straight talk.
